paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss evolution over iterations for five different model configurations, with the y-axis representing "Loss" on a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, and the x-axis representing "#Iteration" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000. The plot includes five distinct lines: a purple solid line labeled "Vanilla", a blue solid line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)", an orange solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64)", a green solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)", a red solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", and a dark blue solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)". All lines begin at a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a rapid initial decline, followed by a slower, more gradual decrease as iterations increase. By approximately 140,000 iterations, all loss values have converged to a stable range between 2.5 and 2.6. The "Vanilla" model starts with the highest loss and ends with the lowest, while the "StrmLLM (n=64)" model begins with a loss of approximately 3.3 and ends with a loss of approximately 2.65. The "SepLLM (n=64)" model begins at a loss of approximately 3.3 and ends at approximately 2.55. The "SepLLM (n=64, H)" model begins at approximately 3.3 and ends at approximately 2.5. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" model begins at approximately 3.3 and ends at approximately 2.5. The "SepLLM (n=128)" model begins at approximately 3.4 and ends at approximately 2.6.
